reason: Runnable (numpy mod-p rank, PARI mathnf; structural metrics dim V_k, det exponent, reach ratio; no wall time) and the S_3 part is far under 20 CPU-min. But as written it does not discriminate. (1) prediction_if_false clause 1 (dim V_k > LM count) is impossible: LM(gh)=LM(g)LM(h) over a field, so an echelon basis of V_k has distinct LMs divisible by LM(f)^k; the pilot 12/12 'dim<=LM' is a unit test of the code, not evidence. Only the equality slack N_k - dim V_k carries information. (2) The 1/32 ceiling needs no experiment: with c(beta)=min(l, max k : LM(f)^k | x^beta) the relaxed objective sum_{beta in M}(c(beta) - delta*|beta|) is separable over monomials, so delta < max_beta c(beta)/|beta| = 1/|LM(f)| = 1/(m*d) = 1/32 for S_5 (LM = prod x_i^8, total degree 32). It is a 5-line proof; compute |LM(f)| combinatorially for S_5 instead. (3) Only clause 2 (non-convex M beating box by >1e-3 at matched l) is empirical, and the design leaves it ill-defined: box values 1/18, 1/10, 0.11905 come from different l/L, finite-l ratios climb toward the asymptote (S_3: JM 1/6, ceiling 1/4), so unmatched comparison is a finite-size artefact; 'box' must be best box over L and aspect at the same l; random subsets are a trivial control (dim V_k ~ 0, lowest ratio) and not a null for the hypothesis. (4) Correctness trap for 'exact ideal-intersection dimensions on non-convex sets': V_k = (f^k) cap F_p[x]_M requires cofactors h whose support is NOT limited to M minus supp(f^k). Cofactor support must be all lattice points of the Minkowski difference conv(M) (-) Newt(f^k) (Newt(hf^k)=Newt(h)+Newt(f^k)). Restricting h to M - shifts undercounts dim V_k and would falsely close class 2. (5) dim V_k only upper-bounds the true graded piece (L_j subset V_{l-j}: reduction mod p of a lattice vector is in V but not every V element lifts), so det >= p^{sum(|M|-dim V_k)} with equality unproven; reach computed from dim V_k is an UPPER bound on reach (right direction for a ceiling, wrong for claiming non-convex M 'beats' box). The mathnf check at L<=4 must test equality of exponents, otherwise a positive 'beats box' is not a lattice reach. (6) S_4 toy L<=8, l<=2 is degenerate: S_4 has degree 4 per variable, f^2 degree 8 per variable, box [0..8]^3 admits only h=const for k=2 (V_2 = span f^2, dim 1) so no shape effect is testable; useful S_4 needs L>=12 (13^3=2197 to 17^3=4913 columns), dense mod-p elimination ~1e11 ops/M ~ minutes each, so only a handful of M fit in 20 min. (7) Transfer to n=131: the LM ceiling transfers exactly (dimension-free, p-free, only |LM(S_5)|=32 enters). The non-convex-vs-box gain does not transfer from m=2,3 to m=4; S_5 exact dim V_k is infeasible here (4 vars, deg 8 each, l=1 box L=16 is 83521 columns). Toy can only report trend of (exact optimum)/(ceiling) over m=2,3 versus box/ceiling = 2/3, 1/2, 2/5 (S_3 1/6 vs 1/4; S_4 1/24 vs 1/12; S_5 1/80 vs 1/32 is box/ceil=0.4). Neither outcome moves B*D^2 or the 0.169 requirement: even the full ceiling 1/32 is 5.4x short of 1/5 and 5.3x short of 0.169; classification: accounting.
